about: SB00's seven plates and the opening vignette, as layout and light comps for the painter (OWNER_NOTES 19 Oct: a human painter over our comps, about 6-7 plates). Coordinates are canvas units of each plate's painting (the frame at rest is 3200 x 1339, the 2.39:1 band of the 3200 x 1800 canvas); delivered pixels are 1.2 per unit (4K). Camera keys and beat times are from the plate's 'at'. Shapes are the block-in; tools/storybook/comps.py renders them.

plates.title: The lamp at the post (opening vignette)

beats.text: Black. Wind over the hills, the river far off.
An old hand strikes a light over a small lamp on a stone sill; the flame catches warm yellow, and its light spreads across the picture.
The light runs on as ink into Plate 1.

plates.prompt: A dark painted illustration. Inside an old stone watch-post at dusk: a deep stone window, the evening sky beyond it deep blue over a dull rose band above dark hills and a pale river far off. On the stone sill a small clay oil lamp. An old man's weathered hand with gray hairs and scarred knuckles and a slate blue-gray wool cuff holds a flint striker over the lamp; the small flame has just caught, warm yellow, lighting the hand and the stone. Everything else in deep shadow. Full-bleed, no border, no text.

plates.title: The cut and the chain

beats.text: Night. On the lip of a great cut in the hill: the Legion's smiths close a man-tall link on an anvil (sparks on the hammer's beat), the standard VII, torches.
"Long ago, the Seventh Legion found something under these hills that wouldn't die,"
The camera descends along the chain and the torch column winding down the cut.
At the bottom, a great stone doorway; inside it, one pale ribbed curve of something vast, faintly glowing. Only that: no face, never the whole.
"and chained it there, in the dark."
The slab slides across the doorway; the pale glow narrows to a line and goes out on the low hit.

plates.prompt: A dark painted illustration looking down into a great cut in a hillside at night. At the top, on the lip of the cut, Roman legionaries in rust-red cloaks and dull bronze crested helmets: two smiths in leather aprons hammer a giant iron chain link on an anvil, sparks flying; a standard with a rust-red banner and the number VII; big burning torches at the top corners. A heavy iron chain with links as tall as a man runs from the anvil down the left wall of the cut into the dark. A long column of small soldiers carrying torches winds down a ramp cut into the right wall. Far below at the bottom of the cut, a massive stone doorway of fitted megaliths with letters carved on its lintel; inside the doorway one smooth pale curved surface with ribs, glowing faintly; a great stone slab stands beside the doorway. Deep shadow, firelight. Full-bleed, no border.

plates.title: Ember

beats.text: Deep under the hills, the Legion's door, buried; the faintest pale glow seeps past it anyway.
"Its light still seeps up through the ground. We call it ember. It burns. It sells. The valley lives by it."
The camera rises with threads of light through rock, gravel and roots: pale deep down, warming to orange-gold near the surface, where they gather as small glowing stones in the soil and the riverbed.
The valley today: the Waystation's roofs where three roads meet, gold lamps in the windows, a hearth, coins passed for a glowing stone, a cart of stones on the road.

plates.prompt: A storybook cross-section illustration, a painted cutaway of the earth under a small valley town at night. At the bottom, deep dark rock and, buried far down, a small ancient stone door with a faint pale light leaking around its edges. Thin threads of light rise slowly up through the dark rock, gravel and roots like sparks rising through water, pale at the bottom and warm orange-gold near the top, where they gather as many small glowing orange stones in the soil and in a riverbed. At the top, above the ground line: stone and timber houses where three roads meet, warm gold lamps in the windows, a hearth glowing through an open door, a market stall where one person hands coins to another for a small glowing stone, a cart of glowing stones on the road, a river at the right, dark hills, a night sky. Full-bleed, no border, no text.

plates.title: The dead get up; first light (MASTER PLATE)

beats.text: Night, frost, a field by a road; ember glints in the soil like coals in ash.
"Where it lies thick, the dead get up after dark." The frost cracks in a line; a dead hand comes up.
"Not them. Just the bodies, full of its light." A body stands, slack and blank-faced, its light at the mouth, the eye sockets and the wounds, like a lamp behind paper.
"Put one down and it spills out." The Watchman's spear; the light pours out onto the frost as small glowing stones; the body falls empty and dark. His breath smokes; theirs never does.
Dawn on the same field (a painted dawn pass): gray, then gold along the hills.

"At first light it sinks into the ground and takes back what it lent. No more than that." The light drains down into the ground; the risen fold onto the frost as plain dead; the stones dim and sink; the Watchman leans on his spear, his lamp guttering. Tilt up to the sun's edge.

plates.prompt: A grim painted illustration, a wide frieze at night on a frosted field beside a road, low dark hills, a dark sky. Small orange embers glint in the frozen soil like coals in ash. Left: the frost has cracked open in a jagged line with orange light inside, and a dead man's hand is coming up out of the crack. Center-left: a dead man stands upright, slack and blank-faced, arms hanging, an orange light glowing inside him that shows at his mouth, his empty eye sockets and his wounds, like a lamp behind paper. Center-right: an old soldier with a gray beard in a slate blue-gray cloak and tabard, a round wooden shield on his arm and a small lamp on his belt, drives a spear into another standing dead man; orange light pours out of the wound and falls onto the frost as a scatter of small glowing stones; the old soldier's breath smokes in the cold. Right: a dead body lying dark and empty on the frost among a few glowing stones. Full-bleed, no border.

plates.title: Keepers and lamps

beats.text: Left, long ago: priests in undyed pale linen lift gold lamps at a river crossing; midstream a lamp is held high and clear of the water, its holder lost in mist; downriver, more crossings, each with a small high light.
"The old priests set keepers at the crossings. After them, the Watch kept the lamps lit. Oil, never ember. Nobody remembers why."
The pan passes behind a dark willow in the foreground: years pass. The grade ages gold into yellow along the pan.
Right, the Watch: a Watchman on a ladder fills a post lamp from an oil jug; the flame yellower and smoky; the water at the crossing dark and smooth, nothing over it.

plates.prompt: A wide painted illustration of one river crossing at night, read left to right. Left: on the near bank four priests in plain undyed pale linen robes lift lamps that burn gold; in the middle of the river a single lamp is held high and clear of the water, whatever holds it hidden in a column of mist; beyond, the river winds away into dark hills past more crossings, each with one small high light. Center: the dark trunk of an old willow in the foreground. Right: years later, the same kind of crossing: an old soldier in a slate blue-gray cloak stands on a wooden ladder against a stone post and pours oil from a jug into an iron lamp on top of the post; the flame is yellow and smoky; the river below is dark and smooth with nothing over it. Full-bleed, no border.

plates.title: The Low Ford; the drowned

beats.text: Close on the Low Ford in winter at night: snow on the banks, ice at the edges; three new black iron cages on posts burn cold blue; midstream a fourth blue light hangs just clear of the water, its holder lost in its glare. Nobody.
"Last winter, somebody lit the lamps at the Low Ford again. Not us. With ember." A slow push toward the fourth light; rings spread under it.
"Now the drowned stand along the ford road, waiting. And something in the water is singing."

The camera pulls back up the road: a wagon on its side; both ditches full of the drowned, standing river-wet, weed in their hair, every face turned to the road. They were there all along. The lamps small beyond the trees; rings on the water under them.

plates.prompt: A grim painted illustration at night in winter, looking down a snowy road to a river ford. In the middle distance the river crosses the road: dark smooth water with ice at the edges and a line of flat stepping stones. On the near bank of the ford stand three new black iron cages on posts with cold blue flames burning inside them, their blue light reflected in the water; in the middle of the river a fourth bright blue light hangs just above the water, nothing visible holding it, rings spreading on the water under it. Bare winter trees on both sides. On the road a broken wagon lies on its side with one wheel in the air. In the ditches on both sides of the road stand rows of drowned dead people, wet, with river weed in their hair, all standing still and facing the road. Snow on the banks. Full-bleed, no border.

plates.title: The traveler

beats.text: Dusk, the last light: deep blue over a dull rose band. A small camp by the ford road: the fire high, a log, a bedroll with its blanket still folded, a pack. The traveler, hood up, back to us, a flask on a cord at the wrist, reads a folded letter. Far up the road, the Waystation's lamps, one higher. Low through the trees by the water, three points of blue.
"Lamps are lit. Stay where they reach."

The traveler folds the letter into the coat, stands, and walks away from us toward the water, out of the fire's warm ring into blue (the music stops as they step out of the light). The camera follows at a walk.
The river, smooth as a mirror: the traveler kneels on the flat stones at the edge, three-quarters from behind, and holds the flask under. Three blue lamps upstream.

plates.prompt: A painted illustration at dusk, the last light: a deep blue sky over a dull rose band on the horizon. Left: a small camp beside a dirt road: a campfire burning high, a log, a bedroll unrolled with a folded blanket on it, a pack; a lone traveler in a long dark hooded wool coat sits on the log with the hood up, seen from behind, reading a folded letter by the firelight. Far up the road in the distance, the small warm lamps of a town, one lamp higher than the rest. Right: the ground slopes down out of the firelight into cold blue shadow to a river as smooth as a mirror with flat stones at its edge; the same hooded traveler kneels on the stones at the water's edge, seen from behind, holding a flask under the water; upstream, three small blue lights glow low through dark trees. Full-bleed, no border.

plates.title: The water

beats.text: No words, no music from here. Close on the water: the traveler's reflection, the face lost in hood and ripple; the surface trembles; rings from the flask.
Blue light slides into the reflection from the river side and grows over the reflected face until it erases it.

The hooded head lifts (seen from behind and to the side); blue washes over the hood's edge. The lamp hangs a hand's breadth above the water, level with the hood, its holder lost in its glare. The lamp never touches the river. The flask still in hand.
The camera tips into the water (the underwater insert): black-green, bubbles rushing up, the blue lamp warped above the surface. Then black over 2 s, to 1:29.5.

plates.prompt: A dark painted illustration, close at a river's edge at the last of dusk. A traveler in a dark wool hooded coat kneels on flat wet stones at the left, seen from behind and to the side, leaning down over the water with the hood up and the face hidden, a gloved hand holding a flask under the water, small rings spreading. Below, in the smooth black water, the traveler's hooded reflection, the face lost in shadow and ripples. To the right, just above the surface, a cold bright blue lamp glares a hand's breadth above the water and level with the hood, so bright that whatever holds it is hidden; its blue light washes the edge of the hood and streaks across the water. Full-bleed, no border.
